text: Let arg(z) represent the principal argument of the complex number z. Then, |z| = 3 and arg(z $-$ 1) $-$ arg(z + 1) = $\frac{π}{4}$ intersect :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $z=x+iy$

$\therefore$ $|z|=\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}$

Given, $|z|=3$

$\therefore$ $\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}=3$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}=9=3^{2}$

This represents a circle with center at (0, 0) and radius = 3

Now, given

$\arg (z-1)-\arg (z+1)=\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \arg (x+iy-1)-\arg (x+iy+1)=\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \arg (x-1+iy)-\arg (x+1+iy)=\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{y}{x-1}\right )-\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{y}{x+1}\right )=\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{\frac{y}{x-1}-\frac{y}{x+1}}{1+\frac{y}{x-1}\times \frac{y}{x+1}}\right )=\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{\frac{xy+y-xy+y}{x2-1}}{\frac{x2-1+y2}{x2-1}}\right )=\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{xy+y-xy+y}{x^{2}-1+y^{2}}\right )=\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2y}{x^{2}-1+y^{2}}=\tan \left (\frac{π}{4}\right )$

$\Rightarrow 2y=x^{2}+y^{2}-1$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}-2y-1=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}+(y-1)^{2}=(\sqrt{2})^{2}$

This represents a circle with center at (0, 1) and radius $\sqrt{2}$.


[IMG]


From diagram you can see both the circles do not cut anywhere.

text:
Let f be a real valued continuous function on [0, 1] and $f(x)=x+\int\limits _{0}^{1}(x-t)f(t)dt$.

Then, which of the following points (x, y) lies on the curve y = f(x) ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$f(x)=x+\int\limits _{0}^{1}(x-t)f(t)dt$

$=x+x\int\limits _{0}^{1}f(t)dt-\int\limits _{0}^{1}tf(t)dt$

$=x\left (1+\int\limits _{0}^{1}f(t)dt\right )-\int\limits _{0}^{1}tf(t)dt$

Now,

let $A=1+\int\limits _{0}^{1}f(t)dt$

and $B=\int\limits _{0}^{1}tf(t)dt$

$\therefore$ $f(x)=Ax-B$

$\Rightarrow f(t)=At-B$

So, $A=1+\int\limits _{0}^{1}f(t)dt$

$=1+\int\limits _{0}^{1}(At-B)dt$

$=1+\left [\frac{At^{2}}{2}-Bt\right ]_{0}^{1}$

$=1+\frac{A}{2}-B$

$\Rightarrow \frac{A}{2}=1-B$ ...... (1)

$B=\int\limits _{0}^{1}tf(t)dt$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{1}t(At-B)dt$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{1}(At^{2}-Bt)dt$

$=\left [\frac{At^{3}}{3}-\frac{Bt^{2}}{2}\right ]_{0}^{1}$

$=\frac{A}{3}-\frac{B}{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{3B}{2}=\frac{A}{3}$ ....... (2)

Solving equation (1) and (2) we get,

$A=\frac{18}{13}$ and $B=\frac{4}{13}$

$\therefore$ $f(x)=\frac{18}{13}x-\frac{4}{13}$

By checking all the options you can see when x = 6 we get

$y=f(x)=\frac{18}{13}\times 6-\frac{4}{13}$

$=\frac{108-4}{13}=8$

$\therefore$ Point (6, 8) lies on the curve.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$\int\limits _{0}^{2}\left (\sqrt{2x}-\sqrt{2x-x^{2}}\right )dx=\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (1-\sqrt{1-y^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right )dy+\int\limits _{1}^{2}\left (2-\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right )dy+I$

Now,

$L.H.S.=\int\limits _{0}^{2}\left (\sqrt{2x}-\sqrt{2x-x^{2}}\right )dx$

$=\sqrt{2}\int\limits _{0}^{2}x^{1/2}dx-\int\limits _{0}^{2}\sqrt{-(x^{2}-2x)}dx$

$=\sqrt{2}\left [\frac{x^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2}}\right ]_{0}^{2}-\int\limits _{0}^{2}\sqrt{-\left [(x-1)^{2}-1\right ]}dx$

$=\sqrt{2}\times \frac{2}{3}\left [2^{\frac{3}{2}}\right ]-\int\limits _{0}^{2}\sqrt{1-(x-1)^{2}}dx$

[We know,

$\int \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}dx=\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}+\frac{a^{2}}{2}\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{x}{a}\right )+C$]

$=\frac{2\sqrt{2}\times 2\sqrt{2}}{3}-\left [\frac{x-1}{2}\sqrt{1-(x-1)^{2}}+\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{x-1}{1}\right )\right ]_{0}^{2}$

$=\frac{8}{3}-\left [\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{1-1}+\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}(1)-\left (\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )\sqrt{1-1}+\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}(-1)\right )\right ]$

$=\frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}\left (\sin \frac{π}{2}\right )+\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}\left (\sin \left (-\frac{π}{2}\right )\right )$

$=\frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{2}.\frac{π}{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\left (-\frac{π}{2}\right )$

$=\frac{8}{3}-\frac{π}{4}-\frac{π}{4}$

$=\frac{8}{3}-\frac{2π}{4}$

$=\frac{8}{3}-\frac{π}{2}$

Now in R.H.S.,

$\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (1-\sqrt{1-y^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right )dy$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{1}dy-\int\limits _{0}^{1}\sqrt{1-y^{2}}-\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{y^{2}}{2}dy$

$=[y]_{0}^{1}-\left [\frac{y}{2}\sqrt{1-y^{2}}+\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{y}{1}\right )\right ]_{0}^{1}-\left [\frac{y^{3}}{6}\right ]_{0}^{1}$

$=1-\left [\left (\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{1-0}+\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}(1)\right )-\left (0+\sin ^{-1}(0)\right )\right ]-\frac{1}{6}$

$=1-\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}\left (\sin \frac{π}{2}\right )-\frac{1}{6}$

$=1-\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{π}{2}-\frac{1}{6}$

$=\frac{5}{6}-\frac{π}{4}$

Now,

$\int\limits _{1}^{2}\left (2-\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right )dy$

$=\left [2y-\frac{y^{3}}{6}\right ]_{1}^{2}$

$=\left [\left (4-\frac{8}{6}\right )-\left (2-\frac{1}{6}\right )\right ]$

$=4-\frac{8}{6}-2+\frac{1}{6}$

$=2-\frac{7}{6}$

$=\frac{5}{6}$

$\therefore$ $R.H.S.=\frac{5}{6}-\frac{π}{4}+\frac{5}{6}+I$

As $L.H.S.=R.H.S.$

$\Rightarrow \frac{8}{3}-\frac{π}{2}=\frac{10}{6}-\frac{π}{4}+I$

$\Rightarrow \frac{10}{6}-\frac{8}{3}+I=-\frac{π}{2}+\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{-6}{6}+I=-\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow I=1-\frac{π}{4}$

From option (c)

$\int\limits _{0}^{1}(1-\sqrt{1-y^{2}})dy$

$=[y]_{0}^{1}-\int\limits _{0}^{1}(\sqrt{1-y^{2}})dy$

$=1-\left [\frac{y}{2}\sqrt{1-y^{2}}+\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{y}{1}\right )\right ]_{0}^{1}$

$=1-\left [\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{1-1}+\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}(1)-\left (0+\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}(0)\right )\right ]$

$=1-\left [\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{π}{2}-0\right ]$

$=1-\frac{π}{4}=I$

$\therefore$ Option (c) is the right answer.

Note :

There is no way to guess which option is correct. You have to check all the options to see which give value equal to I.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text: If y = y(x) is the solution of the differential equation $\left (1+e^{2x}\right )\frac{dy}{dx}+2\left (1+y^{2}\right )e^{x}=0$ and y (0) = 0, then $6\left (y^{'}(0)+\left (y\left (\log _{e}\sqrt{3}\right )\right )^{2}\right )$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$(1+e^{2x})\frac{dy}{dx}+2(1+y^{2})e^{x}=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{-2(1+y^{2})e^{x}}{1+e^{2x}}$

$\Rightarrow \int \frac{dy}{1+y^{2}}=\int \frac{-2e^{x}dx}{(1+e^{2x})}$

$\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}(y)=\int \frac{-2e^{x}dx}{(1+e^{2x})}$

Now,

Let $e^{x}=t$

$\Rightarrow e^{x}dx=dt$

$\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}(y)=\int \frac{-2dt}{1+t^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}(y)=-2\tan ^{-1}(t)+C$

$\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}(y)=-2\tan ^{-1}(e^{x})+C$ [Putting value of t]

Given, y(0) = 0 means when x = 0 the y = 0

$\therefore$ $\tan ^{-1}(0)=-2\tan ^{-1}(e^{o})+C$

$\Rightarrow 0=-2\times \frac{π}{4}+C$

$\Rightarrow C=\frac{π}{2}$

$\therefore$ $\tan ^{-1}(y)=2\tan ^{-1}(e^{x})+\frac{π}{2}$

$\Rightarrow y=\tan \left (-2\tan ^{-1}(e^{x})+\frac{π}{2}\right )$

Differentiating both sides, we get

$y^{'}=\sec ^{2}\left (-2\tan ^{-1}(e^{x})+\frac{π}{2}\right )-2.\frac{e^{x}}{1+e^{2x}}$

$=\sec ^{2}\left (-2\tan ^{-1}(e^{x})+\frac{π}{2}\right )\times \frac{-2e^{x}}{1+e^{2x}}$

$\therefore$ $y^{'}(0)=\sec ^{2}\left (-2\tan ^{-1}(e^{o})+\frac{π}{2}\right )\times \frac{-2e^{o}}{1+e^{o}}$

$=\sec ^{2}\left (-2\times \frac{π}{4}+\frac{π}{2}\right )\times \frac{-2}{2}$

$=\sec ^{2}(0)x-1$

$=1\times 1$

$=-1$

And

$y\left (\log _{e}^{\sqrt{3}}\right )=\tan \left (-2\tan ^{-1}\left (e^{\log _{e}^{\sqrt{3}}}\right )+\frac{π}{2}\right )$

$=\tan \left (-2\tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{3})+\frac{π}{2}\right )$

$=\tan \left (-2\times \frac{π}{3}+\frac{π}{2}\right )$

$=\tan \left (-\frac{π}{6}\right )$

$=-\tan \left (\frac{π}{6}\right )$

$=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$\therefore$ $6\left (y^{'}(0)+\left (y(\log _{e}^{\sqrt{3}})\right )^{2}\right )$

$=6\left (-1+\left (\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )^{2}\right )$

$=6\left (-1+\frac{1}{3}\right )=6\times \frac{-2}{3}=-4$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text: Let a triangle ABC be inscribed in the circle $x^{2}-\sqrt{2}(x+y)+y^{2}=0$ such that $\angle BAC=\frac{π}{2}$. If the length of side AB is $\sqrt{2}$, then the area of the $\Delta$ABC is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Note:

For equation of circle $x^{2}+y^{2}+2gx+2fy+c=0$, center is $(-g,\qquad -f)$ and radius $r=\sqrt{g^{2}+f^{2}-c}$

Given,

equation of circle is

$x^{2}-\sqrt{2}(x+y)+y^{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}-\sqrt{2}x-\sqrt{2}y=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}+2\left (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )x+2\left (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )y=0$

$\therefore$ $g=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $f=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\therefore$ Center $=(-g,-f)=\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )$

And Radius $=r=\sqrt{\left (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )^{2}+\left (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )^{2}-0}$

$=\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1$


[IMG]


As AB and AC makes an angle 90${}^{\circ }$ then line BC passes through the center of circle and BC is the diameter of the circle.

$\therefore$ Length of BC = 2r = 2 $\times$ 1 = 2

$\therefore$ $AC^{2} = BC^{2}$ $-$ $AB^{2}$

$= 2^{2}$ $-$ ($\sqrt{2})^{2}$

= 2

$\Rightarrow$ AC = $\sqrt{2}$

$\therefore$ Area of right angle triangle ABC

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ AC $\times$ AB

= $\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ $\sqrt{2}$ $\sqrt{2}$

= 1 square unit.

text: The distance of the origin from the centroid of the triangle whose two sides have the equations $x-2y+1=0$ and $2x-y-1=0$ and whose orthocenter is $\left (\frac{7}{3},\frac{7}{3}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
[IMG]


For point A,

2x $-$ y $-$ 1 = 0 ...... (1)

x $-$ 2y + 1 = 0 ...... (2)

Solving (1) and (2), we get

x = 1, y = 1.

$\therefore$ Point A = (1, 1)

Altitude from B to line AC is perpendicular to line AC.

$\therefore$ Equation of altitude BH is

2x + y + $λ$ = 0 ...... (3)

It passes through point $H\left (\frac{7}{3},\frac{7}{3}\right )$ so it satisfy the equation (3).

$\frac{14}{3}+\frac{7}{3}+λ=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = $-$7

$\therefore$ Altitude BH = 2x + y $-$ 7 = 0 ...... (4)

Solving equation (1) and (4), we get

x = 2, y = 3.

$\therefore$ Point B = (2, 3)

Altitude from C to line AB is perpendicular to line AB.

$\therefore$ Equation of altitude CH is

x + 2y + $λ$ = 0 ...... (5)

It passes through point $H\left (\frac{7}{3},\frac{7}{3}\right )$ so it satisfy equation (5).

$\frac{7}{3}+\frac{14}{3}+λ=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = $-$7

$\therefore$ Altitude CH = x + 2y $-$ 7 = 0 ...... (6)

Solving equation (2) and (6), we get

x = 3, y = 2

$\therefore$ Point C = (3, 2)

Centroid G (x, y) of triangle A (1, 1), B (2, 3) and C (3, 2) is

$x=\frac{1+2+3}{3}=2$, $y=\frac{1+2+3}{3}=2$

Now, distance of point G (2, 2) from center O (0, 0) is

$OG=\sqrt{2^{2}+2^{2}}=2\sqrt{2}$

text: The number of values of a $\in$ N such that the variance of 3, 7, 12, a, 43 $-$ a is a natural number is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

5 numbers are 3, 7, 12, a, 43 $-$ a

$\therefore$ Mean $(x–)=\frac{3+7+12+a+43-a}{5}$

$=\frac{65}{5}$

$=13$

We know,

Variance $(σ^{2})=\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{n}-(x–)^{2}$

$=\frac{3^{2}+7^{2}+12^{2}+a^{2}+(43-a)^{2}}{5}-(13)^{2}$

$=\frac{9+49+144+a^{2}+1849+a^{2}-86a}{5}-169$

$=\frac{2a^{2}-86a+2051}{5}-169$

$=\frac{2a^{2}-86a+2051-845}{5}$

$=\frac{2a^{2}-86a+1206}{5}$

$=\frac{2}{5}(a^{2}-43a+603)$

Variance will be natural number if $a^{2}-43a+603$ is a multiple of 5.

$\therefore$ $a^{2}-43a+603=5n$

$\Rightarrow a^{2}-43a+603-5n=0$ ..... (1)

$\therefore$ $a=\frac{43\pm \sqrt{D}}{2}$

Now "a" will be natural number if

(1) D is a perfect square and

(2) $43\quad \pm \sqrt{D}$ is multiple of 2

From equation (1),

$D=(-43)^{2}-4.1.(603-5n)$

$=1849-2412+20n$

$=20n-563$

For any value of n, unit digit of 20n is always 0. Then 20n $-$ 563 will give a number whose unit digit is 7.

For perfect square numbers ex : $1^{2} = 1, 2^{2} = 4, 3^{2} = 9, 4^{2} = 16, 5^{2} = 25, 6^{2} = 36, 7^{2} = 49, 8^{2} = 64, 9^{2} = 81, 10^{2} = 100$

So, unit digit is either 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9; it can't be 7. So D can't be perfect square.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text: Let y = y(x), x > 1, be the solution of the differential equation $(x-1)\frac{dy}{dx}+2xy=\frac{1}{x-1}$, with $y(2)=\frac{1+e^{4}}{2e^{4}}$. If $y(3)=\frac{e^{α}+1}{βe^{α}}$, then the value of $α+β$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}+y\left (\frac{2x}{x-1}\right )=\frac{1}{(x-1)^{2}}$

$\text{I.F}=e^{\int \frac{2x}{x-1}dx}$

$\begin{array}{l} =e^{2\int \left (\frac{x-1}{x-1}+\frac{1}{x-1}\right )dx} \\  \\ =e^{2x+2\ln (x-1)} \\  \\ =\mathrm{e}^{2x}(\mathrm{x}-1)^{2} \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow \int d\left (y\cdot e^{2x}(x-1)^{2}\right )=\int e^{2x}dx$

$\Rightarrow \quad y\cdot e^{2x}(x-1)^{2}=\frac{e^{2x}}{2}+c$

$↓y(2)=\frac{1+e^{4}}{2e^{4}}$

$\frac{1+e^{4}}{2e^{4}}\cdot e^{4}=\frac{e^{4}}{2}+c$

$\Rightarrow \quad c=\frac{e^{4}}{2}\left (\frac{1+e^{4}-e^{4}}{e^{4}}\right )=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow \quad y\cdot e^{2x}(x-1)^{2}=\frac{e^{2x}+1}{2}$

$↓y(3)=\frac{e^{α}+1}{βe^{α}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{e^{α}+1}{βe^{α}}\cdot e^{6}\cdot 4=\frac{e^{6}+1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow α=6$ and $β=8\Rightarrow α+β=14$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text: Let 3, 6, 9, 12, ....... upto 78 terms and 5, 9, 13, 17, ...... upto 59 terms be two series. Then, the sum of the terms common to both the series is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
1st AP :

3, 6, 9, 12, ....... upto 78 terms

$t_{78} = 3 + (78$ $-$ 1)3

= 3 + 77 $\times$ 3

= 234

2nd AP :

5, 9, 13, 17, ...... upto 59 terms

$t_{59} = 5 + (59$ $-$ 1)4

= 5 + 58 $\times$ 4

= 237

Common term's AP :

First term = 9

Common difference of first AP = 3

And common difference of second AP = 4

$\therefore$ Common difference of common terms

AP = LCM (3, 4) = 12

$\therefore$ New AP = 9, 21, 33, .......

$t_{n} = 9 + (n$ $-$ 1)12 $\leq$ 234

$\Rightarrow n\leq \frac{237}{12}$

$\Rightarrow n=19$

$\therefore$ $S_{19}=\frac{19}{2}[2.9+(19-1)12]$

$=19(9+108)$

$=2223$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text:
For real numbers a, b (a > b > 0), let

Area $\left \{(x,y):x^{2}+y^{2}\leq a^{2}\text{and}\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}\geq 1\right \}=30π$ 

and

Area $\left \{(x,y):x^{2}+y^{2}\geq b^{2}\text{and}\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}\leq 1\right \}=18π$

Then, the value of (a $-$ $b)^{2}$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{2}+y^{2}\leq a^{2}$ is interior of circle

and $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}\geq 1$ is exterior of ellipse


[IMG]


$\therefore$ Area $=πa^{2}-πab=30π$

Similarly $x^{2}+y^{2}\geq b^{2}$ and $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}\leq 1$ gives

$πab-πb^{2}=18π$

By (1) and (2), $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{5}{3}\Rightarrow a=\frac{5b}{3}$

$\Rightarrow π\cdot \frac{25b^{2}}{9}-π\cdot \frac{5b^{2}}{3}=30π$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{25}{9}-\frac{5}{3}\right )b^{2}=30$

$\Rightarrow \frac{10}{9}b^{2}=30\Rightarrow b^{2}=27$

and $a^{2}=\frac{25}{9}\cdot 27=75$

$(a-b)^{2}=(5\sqrt{3}-3\sqrt{3})^{2}=3\cdot 4=12$

text: Let the coefficients of $x^{-1}$ and $x^{-3}$ in the expansion of $\left (2x^{\frac{1}{5}}-\frac{1}{x^{\dfrac{1}{5}}}\right )^{15},x>0$, be m and n respectively. If r is a positive integer such that $mn^{2}={}^{15}C_{r}.2^{r}$, then the value of r is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, Binomial expansion

$\left (2x^{\frac{1}{5}}-\frac{1}{x^{\dfrac{1}{5}}}\right )^{15}$

$\therefore$ General Term

$T_{r+1}={}^{15}C_{r}.\left (2x^{\frac{1}{5}}\right )^{15-r}.\left (-\frac{1}{x^{\dfrac{1}{5}}}\right )^{r}$

$={}^{15}C_{r}.2^{15-r}.x^{\frac{1}{5}(15-r-r)}.(-1)^{r}$

For $x^{-1}$ term;

$\frac{1}{5}(15-2r)=-1$

$\Rightarrow 15-2r=-5$

$\Rightarrow 2r=20$

$\Rightarrow r=10$

m is the coefficient of $x^{-1}$ term,

$\therefore$ $m={}^{15}C_{10}.2^{15-10}.(-1)^{10}$

$={}^{15}C_{10}.2^{5}$

For $x^{-3}$ term;

$\frac{1}{5}(15-2r)=-3$

$\Rightarrow 15-2r=-15$

$\Rightarrow 2r=30$

$\Rightarrow r=15$

n is the coefficient of $x^{-3}$ term,

$\therefore$ $n={}^{15}C_{15}.2^{15-15}.(-1)^{15}$

$=1.\qquad 1.-1$

$=-1$

Given,

$mn^{2}={}^{15}C_{r}.2^{r}$

$\Rightarrow {}^{15}C_{10}.2^{5}.(1)^{2}={}^{15}C_{r}.2^{r}$ [putting value of m and n]

$\Rightarrow {}^{15}C_{15-10}.2^{5}={}^{15}C_{r}.2^{r}$

$\Rightarrow {}^{15}C_{5}.2^{5}={}^{15}C_{r}.2^{r}$

Comparing both side, we get

$r=5$.

text: The total number of four digit numbers such that each of first three digits is divisible by the last digit, is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
If unit digit is 1 then $\to 9\times$ s $10\times 10=900$ numbers 

If unit digit is 2 then $\to 4\times 5\times 5=100$ numbers 

If unit digit is 3 then $\to 3\times 4\times 4=48$ numbers

 If unit digit is 4 then $\to 2\times 3\times 3=18$ numbers

 If unit digit is 5 then $\to 1\times 2\times 2=4$ numbers 

If unit digit is 6 then $\to 1\times 2\times 2=4$ numbers

For $7,8,9\to 4+4+4=12$ Numbers

Total $=1086$ Numbers
